data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A compiled program executes with perfect fidelity on digital hardware; a non-expert panel introduces stochastic execution errors, reading-comprehension failures, and aggregation noise, so 'fidelity' is not guaranteed.","A program's causal completeness can be formally verified against a specification; a checklist's causal completeness typically cannot, because real-world tasks lack a formal specification and the 'frozen theory' is informal natural-language procedure.","A program is rigid and cannot adapt to novel inputs outside its specification; a human expert's mutable theory can, so the expert retains an advantage on distributional shift that a compiled artifact lacks."],"overturn_conditions":["If the checklist is explicitly a surface heuristic and does not purport to encode causal structure, the program-completeness analogy fails and the distinction between compliance and genuine reasoning is not moot but central.","If the panel's execution fidelity is so low that it introduces more noise than the frozen-theory advantage, the panel cannot outperform the expert regardless of theory quality, breaking the decomposition.","If a single evaluation cannot distinguish causal completeness from distribution-specific surface fit (as SCR_002 worries), then the program-correctness analogy overclaims: even property-based tests within one distribution cannot rule out distribution-specific luck, and cross-distribution evidence is required by necessity."],"shared_structure":["Both a compiled program and a checklist encode a prior causal/theoretic model in a fixed procedural form that is then executed faithfully by an agent who may not understand the underlying model.","In both cases, the reliability of the output depends on (theory-quality of the fixed artifact) \u00d7 (execution-fidelity by the operator), rather than on the operator's own expertise.","When the fixed artifact is deductively complete for the task class, compliance with the artifact and genuine reasoning about the task converge: there is no additional latent reasoning the operator needs to supply."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["If a checklist is a frozen theory analogous to a compiled program, then evaluating the checklist's causal completeness (does it capture structure or surface correlations?) is equivalent to evaluating the program's specification-correctness \u2014 and adversarial items are the analogue of property-based test cases designed to separate correct implementations from implementations that pass on the evaluated distribution but fail on edge cases.","The distinction between 'genuine reliability' and 'compliance that tracks the right answer' maps to the distinction between 'the program is correct' and 'the program passes the test suite'; a single evaluation with adversarial probes can distinguish them only if the probes are designed to break surface correlations, just as property-based tests target edge cases."]},"claim":"A non-expert panel using a checklist outperforms a single expert only when the checklist encodes a causally complete or structurally faithful model of the task domain; under that condition, 'checklist compliance' and 'genuine reasoning' coincide rather than diverge, so the problem of distinguishing them partially dissolves.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is a surface heuristic rather than a causal model; in that case, compliance is not genuine reasoning and the distinction remains meaningful.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's mutable internal theory is strictly better-calibrated than the frozen theory (e.g., in a novel domain the checklist has not yet incorporated); then the panel's fidelity advantage is outweighed by theory-quality deficit.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Cross-distribution shifts break the observed\u2192latent edge assumed by the frozen theory (SCR_002); then a single evaluation cannot distinguish genuine gain from distribution-specific luck.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a 'frozen theory' (per SCR_001) that encodes the checklist author's causal model in procedural form. The non-expert panel supplies execution fidelity. If the frozen theory is causally complete, the panel's compliance is the mechanism of reliable judgment. The panel-vs-expert comparison is thus reframed as 'high-fidelity execution of a good frozen theory' vs 'biased execution of a mutable internal theory.' The distinction between genuine reliability gain and mere compliance-tracking collapses if the checklist is deductively complete (SCR_003), because compliance is the correct application of a complete causal model.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
